successCriteria.description: `FakeLeaveRepository` in tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts satisfies the full `ILeaveRepository` contract including `findByReversesRequestId`, returning `null` by default and the previously-created reversal row when one exists; `npm run build` (tsc) is clean with no `any`.

A reversal describe block asserts that after cancelling an APPROVED request the ORIGINAL row still reads `status === LeaveStatus.APPROVED` with `approverId`/`approvalComment`/`decidedAt` byte-identical, and that the original object was never passed to `repository.update` (no update call targets the original id).
The reversal test asserts a NEW row is created via `repository.create` with `status === LeaveStatus.CANCELLED` and `reversesRequestId === original.id`.

The reversal test asserts the new row copies `employeeId`, `leaveTypeCode`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `requestedDays` and `reason` verbatim from the original, sets `approverId`/`approvalComment`/`submittedAt`/`decidedAt` all to `null`, and sets `cancelledBy === actor.id` with `cancelledAt` set.

The reversal test asserts the balance release happens exactly once on the ORIGINAL's `requestedDays` (`usedDays -= requestedDays`) with `pendingDays` untouched (exactly one balance update call, `pendingDays` undefined in the change set).
The reversal test asserts exactly one `AuditAction.CANCEL` entry with `entityId === original.id`, `beforeState === original`, `afterState === reversal`, and exactly one cancellation notification.

The double-cancel guard test asserts that when `findByReversesRequestId` returns an existing reversal, `cancel` throws `ConflictError` (409) and performs no insert, no balance write, no audit and no notification.
The test asserts DRAFT/SUBMITTED cancellation stays in place: no reversal row is created and `reversesRequestId` remains `null` on the cancelled row.

Containment-based transaction assertions prove all reversal steps occur inside the single `withTransaction` callback (`uow.callCount === 1`) with the stub `PoolClient` forwarded to every participating call (create, balance update, audit, notification, and the reversal lookup).
The full suite passes via `npm run build && npx jest --passWithNoTests --forceExit` with the existing APPROVED cancel tests still green.

constraints: EDIT ONLY tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts. No production source edits (leave.model.ts, leave.repository.ts, leave.service.ts, web/src/shared/types/index.ts are fixed contracts to read, not modify).
Reuse the existing eight in-memory fakes and the existing fixtures (makeRequest, makeActor, makeBalance, makeEmployee, makePolicy); extend the existing suite rather than creating a parallel one.

Do not assume field/method names — read them from the fixed contracts before writing assertions (LeaveRequest.reversesRequestId, ILeaveRepository.findByReversesRequestId, LeaveRequestView.reversesRequestId).
Reversal tests must seed the balance with usedDays = REQUESTED_DAYS (the existing cancel beforeEach seeds usedDays: 0, which would not exercise the release path).
Strict TypeScript: no `any`; the fake must still structurally satisfy ILeaveRepository (no `as any` casts to bypass the interface).
Verification command is `npm run build && npx jest --passWithNoTests --forceExit` (per HARNESS.json).
outOfScope: scripts/smoke.js reversal assertion — owned by sibling sub-phase 4b; do not create or gate on it.
Any production source change (leave.service.ts, leave.repository.ts, leave.model.ts, web/src/shared/types/index.ts) — the Phase 1–3 deliverables are fixed contracts.
New endpoints, route changes, or web test changes.
Integration/e2e tests against real Postgres (the UNIQUE-index backstop is exercised by the smoke script, not this unit suite).

entityInvariants.invariant: Once APPROVED, the row is terminal and immutable: status/approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt are never written again. Cancelling it must not pass the original object to repository.update.

entityInvariants.entity: LeaveRequestReversal (domain role of LeaveRequest, not a separate table)
entityInvariants.invariant: Born CANCELLED and terminal/inert: never transitions, reserves nothing, is never itself reversed. Carries reversesRequestId = original id and copies employeeId/leaveTypeCode/startDate/endDate/requestedDays/reason verbatim with approverId/approvalComment/submittedAt/decidedAt null.
Cancellation of an APPROVED request releases the original's requestedDays from usedDays exactly once (usedDays -= requestedDays, no pro-rating); pendingDays is untouched.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null when no reversal exists (repository does not throw); the service decides error semantics. Fake must return null by default and the previously-created reversal when set.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Only the direct manager or an ADMIN may cancel an APPROVED request; owner cancelling own APPROVED is ForbiddenError; guards run before the transaction.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws ConflictError (409) when a reversal already exists (double-cancel) or when startDate <= today (UTC day); no insert/balance write/audit/notification on the guard path.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The fake's findByReversesRequestId signature and return semantics must match the interface exactly (returns null when absent, the reversal row when present).
Assertions on the reversal row's fields must match the canonical LeaveRequest shape (reversesRequestId is the last field; CreateLeaveRequestInput = Omit<LeaveRequest,'id'> so create supplies it).
Assertions on the reversal branch's behaviour (audit entityId/beforeState/afterState, balance release, double-cancel guard, DRAFT/SUBMITTED in-place) must match the implemented cancel branch.
The read-model field asserted for wire honesty (LeaveRequestView.reversesRequestId) must match the web shared types.
The reversal invariants asserted must match the reconciled GP-008 rules (immutability, new-instance reversal, exactly-once release, single CANCEL audit, double-cancel guard).

integrationPoints.why: Must satisfy ILeaveRepository including findByReversesRequestId so the service's reversal branch and double-cancel guard are exercisable.
The suite asserts the branch's observable behaviour (reversal insert, balance release, audit, notification, guard) through the injected fakes.
The fake's method signature must match this interface exactly for the suite to compile under strict TS.
Containment assertions rely on the FakeUnitOfWork stub client being forwarded to every participating call.
